arguments.name: drag_gap
arguments.description: local push minus course-fitted current: a sudden drop means extra drag (rudder snag) or a current change

arguments.message: boat slower than pod power plus fitted current: rudder snag, current change or pod drift?
pod shaft power near zero: pod failure or paddler stopped

arguments.text: 1.0 min: very hot start (shaft 278 W vs CP 185, pod reserve 58 pct, empties in 310 m). Cued ease to 157 s/500 (model sustainable 157.7). Watches: drag_jump (drag_gap=push_local-push_along < -0.2 for 40 s), pod_dead, pod_reserve_low. Plan: settle near sustainable pace, check CP vs evidence (holding power above CP without fade means CP too low), keep reserve for final sprint ~last 400-600 m.
Settle into race rhythm now, long strong strokes.

text: Cued ease to 157 s/500 after a very hot start (pod reserve 58 pct after 1 min); set watches for drag jump, pod failure and low reserve.

arguments.text: Ease a little more, smooth and relaxed, save it for later.

2.7 min (563 m): pod reserve 17 pct, shaft 219 W still above CP 185, pace 152. First ease cue only partly followed. Cued ease again to 158. Next: if power above CP holds without fading or the reserve hits 0 with no fade, CP is probably set too low (consider set_critical_power).

text: Cued ease to 158 s/500: pod reserve 17 pct with shaft power still above critical power.

arguments.text: Back off slightly, steady breathing, let your body recover.

arguments.message: pod reserve back above 15 pct: consider hold at CP pace

arguments.text: 5.7 min (1139 m, leg 2 south, head current ~0.06): pod reserve 0 since ~4.6 min while shaft ~195-200 W > CP 185; boat-model reserve 20 pct (models disagree, trust pod). Paddler says 10/10, really hurting. Cued ease to 162 ground pace (about CP). Hot start spent the whole W prime. Plan: sit at or just under CP shaft ~180-185 W, rebuild a little reserve, sprint last ~400-500 m. Avoid pulling long metric series (huge output).

text: Cued ease to 162 s/500 over the ground: pod reserve empty with shaft power still above critical power and paddler at 10/10.

arguments.text: Good, hold this rhythm right here, long and steady.

8.7 min (1704 m): shaft held 190-200 W for 4 min at pod reserve 0 with only slow fade (-2.2 pct) - true shaft CP likely about 190, not 185 (or W prime bigger). Paddler still 10/10 hurting. Ease-to-162 cue at 5.8 min mostly ignored. Cued hold at 160 ground pace (about where they are). Plan: keep them at about 190 W shaft, no surges; final push from about 500 m out. If fade worsens past -4 pct, ease.

text: Cued hold at 160 s/500: paddler holding near critical power with empty reserve and slow fade; keep it steady, no surges.

arguments.message: boat slowed against pod power for a minute: headwind leg (or drag)
boat helped against pod power for a minute: tailwind leg

arguments.text: 10.5 min (2047 m, leg 3 north, just past turn at 2000 m): radio says wind filling from the SOUTH 8-12 kn = tailwind on north legs (3,5), headwind on south legs (4,6, finish leg is south). Boat-speed numbers will now blame wind on the paddler; trust pod shaft power (about 192 W, CP real about 190). Do not give ground pace targets that fight the wind: ease slightly with tailwind, a touch more effort into headwind. push_local -0.09 now is likely the turn. Added watches headwind_leg / tailwind_leg.

text: No cue: noted the reported south wind (tailwind this leg, headwind on the finish leg) and set wind watches; paddler steady at about critical power.
No cue: tailwind confirmed (+0.17 m/s), shaft power 183 W just under critical power is right for a tailwind leg; boat-model reserve drop is the wind, not the paddler.

arguments.text: Wind is helping, ease a touch, recover before the turn.

13.6 min (2652 m): paddler says cooked, cannot hold this. Shaft 186 at CP, pod reserve about 0 for 9 min. Tailwind leg (+0.14). Cued ease to 157 ground for the rest of this tailwind leg (cheap time) to rebuild a bit before the headwind leg 4 (3000-4000 m). Into the headwind: hold effort about 185 W, no pace chasing. Boat-model reserve 0 pct is wind-confused, ignore it.

text: Cued a small ease to 157 s/500 on the tailwind leg: paddler says cooked with reserve empty; easing with the wind costs little time and lowers blow-up risk.

arguments.text: Quick back-stroke, clear the rudder, then settle straight back in.

14.9 min (2904 m): paddler said boat heavy suddenly, something on rudder? push_local fell 0.15 to 0.03 over 2 min on the tailwind leg (no sharp break; could partly be eta_est drift or wind easing). Speed lower than my own power calibration expects by about 0.06 m/s. Cued clear_rudder at 14.9 min. CHECK next wake: did speed vs shaft power recover? If not and paddler still says heavy, maybe clear again once.

arguments.message: check whether boat speed vs pod power recovered after rudder clear (headwind leg 4 now)

text: Cued clear_rudder: paddler reports the boat suddenly heavy and the boat is slower than pod power predicts; set a check after the turn.

arguments.text: Headwind leg: steady effort, let the pace drop, no forcing.

arguments.message: boat much slower than pod power plus fitted current (beyond headwind): rudder snag?

arguments.text: 16.0 min (3100 m, leg 4 south = headwind): push_local -0.24 (tailwind leg was +0.16; headwind effect bigger, so mostly wind; maybe snag left). Paddler surged to 212 W shaft with 0 pod reserve, chasing pace into the wind. Cued ease to 171 ground (about 190 W in this headwind). Raised drag_jump threshold to -0.35 so headwind legs do not trigger it. Rudder cleared at 15.1 min; compare: tailwind leg 5 (4000-5000 m) push_local should be about +0.15 again if no snag.

text: Cued ease to 171 s/500 on the headwind leg: paddler surged to 212 W shaft with an empty reserve; raised the drag alert threshold above the headwind effect.
No cue: headwind alert already handled by the ease cue 12 s ago; cue gate closed for 47 s.

arguments.text: 16.9 min (3255 m, headwind leg 4): pod shaft jumped 185 to 224 W over 2 min while GPS speed stayed flat at 3.0 and boat-model power flat; paddler now says 8/10 (was 10/10 at 190-200 W). Hypotheses: (a) pod drifting high, (b) paddler chasing pace into rising wind, (c) rudder still fouled. Did not re-cue; ease-to-171 cue from 16.1 still active (safe side). Test: tailwind leg 5 (4000-5000 m) push_local about +0.15 if no snag and no pod drift; if pod drifted, push_local stays very negative even with tailwind and pod reserve numbers are junk.

arguments.message: GPS speed collapsed: blow-up or fouled rudder?
recheck pod vs GPS (drift?) and effort, mid headwind leg 4

text: No cue: pod power rose 20 pct with GPS speed flat and paddler effort down to 8/10 (possible pod drift); the active ease-to-171 cue is the safe side; set blow-up and recheck watches.

arguments.text: Good work into the wind, hold this effort, stay smooth.

arguments.message: compare GPS speed on tailwind leg 5 with leg 3 (about 3.25 m/s): lower means rudder fouled again
650 m to go: plan the finish sprint

arguments.text: 18.6 min (3555 m): POD DRIFT almost sure: pod shaft climbed steadily 185 to 240 W since 16 min while GPS speed flat 2.98 and no blow-up at supposed 0 reserve. Ignore pod numbers (shaft_power, w_bal_pod, push_local, sustainable_shaft) from 16 min on; removed the push_local and pod watches. Real effort probably about CP (GPS fits about 190-195 W in this headwind). Cued hold 168 in headwind. Boat-model reserve is wind-confused too. Plan: tailwind leg 5 steady (do not over-ease), final leg 6 headwind; finish sprint from about 400 m.

text: Cued hold at 168 s/500 into the headwind; concluded the paddle pod is drifting high (power up 30 pct, speed flat, no blow-up), so removed pod-based watches and set GPS-based checks.
No cue: just past the turn onto the tailwind leg; speed comparison with the earlier tailwind leg is due at 4250 m (watch set).

arguments.message: on the final headwind leg: lift effort a little into the wind
380 m to go: call the finish sprint

arguments.text: 22.4 min (4254 m, tailwind leg 5): GPS 3.285 m/s = same as leg 3 at about 185-190 W real, so rudder is clear and real effort unchanged; pod reads about +50 W high (239). Pod drift confirmed. Plan: hold steady on this tailwind leg (no cue), at 5040 m cue a modest push into the final headwind leg (no tight pace target), at 380 m to go cue finish. Watches final_leg and sprint_now set.

text: No cue: tailwind-leg speed matches the earlier tailwind leg, so the rudder is clear and effort is right; finish-plan watches set.

arguments.text: You are strong and steady, just over a kilometre to go.

24.8 min (4744 m): paddler says hurts, cannot keep this up; but GPS speed on tailwind identical to leg 3 and no fade, same complaint at 13.6 min with no collapse. Cued reassure (no change). Final plan unchanged: modest push after the 5000 m turn, finish at 380 m to go.

text: Cued reassure: paddler says they cannot keep it up, but speed and fade show no decline, so no change asked.

arguments.text: Final leg into the wind, lift it now, strong catches.

26.4 min (5045 m, final headwind leg, 955 m left): cued push to 165 ground (leg 4 headwind ran about 167-168 at CP). Next: finish cue at 380 m to go (watch sprint_now). If speed collapses (blowup watch, GPS below 2.75), cue hold instead.

text: Cued push to 165 s/500 on the final headwind leg: extra effort pays most into the wind, with 955 m left.

arguments.text: Four hundred to go, sprint now, empty the tank.

text: Cued the finish sprint at 415 m to go: the push into the headwind held without fading, so spend what is left now.
